name: NTIRE RAW Reconstruction Challenge (2025)
description: Numerous low-level vision tasks operate in the RAW domain due to its linear properties, bit depth, and sensor designs. Despite this, RAW image datasets are scarce and more expensive to collect than the already large and public sRGB datasets. For this reason, many approaches try to generate realistic RAW images using sensor information and sRGB images. This paper covers the second challenge on RAW Reconstruction from sRGB (Reverse ISP). We aim to recover RAW sensor images from smartphones given the corresponding sRGB images without metadata and, by doing this, ``reverse" the ISP transformation. Over 150 participants joined this NTIRE 2025 challenge and submitted efficient models. The proposed methods and benchmark establish the state-of-the-art for generating realistic RAW data.
general_score_metric: PSNR (primary), supplemented by SSIM and LPIPS
typical_sota_score: ≈30–40 dB (PSNR) depending on dataset and method
reputation: NTIRE challenges are well-regarded within the low-level / computational imaging community and attract many participants, making them a standard venue for comparing state-of-the-art methods.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on low-level vision; limited public RAW datasets make the task challenging; metrics like PSNR/SSIM can be sensitive to alignment, bit-depth and clipping; challenge entries emphasize efficiency as well as fidelity.
